response.consequence: Within the cache TTL, a user who is legitimately allowed to access one resource can be denied because a different resource whose name and folder concatenate to the same string was denied earlier. This is a fail-closed wrong authorization result and is intermittent and hard to diagnose.
response.explanation: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name and parent folder with '_' separators. Name and folder UID are caller-supplied and may contain underscores. Check on (name="a_b", folder="c") and on (name="a", folder="b_c") therefore produce the same key. A denial recorded for one is read back by Check at the top of the function as a denial for the other. That second request returns Allowed:false without any permission evaluation. The key also begins with the same "ns.perm_uid_action" prefix as userPermCacheKey, which is only distinguished by its suffix. The authorization decision is cached under a key that is not injective in its inputs.
response.title: Denial cache key joins free-form fields with '_' and can collide, producing false denials
